title: secp256k1-ecdlp: automorphism-aware Pollard rho v3 (dual look-back cycle detection, epoch limit)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, the single-shot classical automorphism-aware Pollard rho algorithm v3 in proof.md recovers x with success probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^127.633635 total target-group-operation equivalents (time_log2 = 127.633635 = 25526727/200000), including setup, seeding, all walk steps, canonicalization, lazy-representation updates, dual distance-2 and distance-3 fruitless-cycle detection with escapes, epoch-limit reseeds, degenerate reseeds, distinguished-point processing, the explicitly charged post-merge detection allowance (K*2^72 walker-steps, 2^88 units, residual failure probability below 2^-369), extraction, verification and output. The walk runs on the (r-1)/6 classes of the order-6 automorphism group; its per-step cost is one reference batched incomplete affine addition plus 652.3 other instruction equivalents in the worst case (578 direct plus 74.3 amortized escape charge) and involves no per-step mod-r multiplication. Two fruitless-cycle families are handled explicitly: the period-2 negation family (rate ~1/192, charged bound 1/64, census-measured 1/115) and the period-3 order-identity family created by 1+lam+lam^2=0 mod r (rate ~2^-16.7, proven algebraically), both detected by dual look-backs with one-addition escapes; longer zero-sum families of the multiplier ring are bounded below 2^-40 per step by pattern counting and fenced by a per-walker epoch limit of 2^36 steps (any family below 2^-31.4 per step wastes at most the charged 5% slack). Budget: t = 1.15*sqrt((r-1)/6) walker steps over 2^16 distinguished-point walkers; modeled collision probability 0.450 at the charged useful-visit fraction 0.95; table-overflow tail <= exp(-2^58.2) with the correct capacity ratio 0.065. Peak memory is strictly above 2^70 and far below 2^71 bytes, reported as memory_log2_bytes = 70.1; preprocessing is at most 2^25.6 target-group-operation equivalents and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. Classical cold attack; no uncharged advice, quantum steps or amortization over targets. The algebraic structure, the order-3 identity and the lazy-representation invariant are verified exactly at production parameters by experiment.py Part A (96 walk steps); Part B runs the complete v3 attack on a 20-bit j=0 toy curve with the production predicate: 85/200 = 0.425 vs 0.4845 ideal (toy-scale detection lag, analyzed), 335 distance-2 escapes, 0 distance-3 escapes, 0 extraction-verification failures, plus a 40,000-step cycle-return census (distance-2 rate 1/115, distance-3 below census resolution).

experiments.purpose: Part A verifies at full production parameters: the order-6 automorphism identities, the order-3 identity 1+lam+lam^2=0 mod r, G6 closure, the class count (r-1)/6, the pairwise class-disjoint walk-constant setup check, and the lazy-representation invariant along 96 production walk steps. Part B runs the complete v3 attack on a 20-bit j=0 toy curve (lazy representations, dual distance-2/3 look-back cycle detection with fruitless/useful discrimination, one-addition escapes, epoch limit, low-bits distinguished points, capped table, canonical-frame extraction) and a 40,000-step cycle-return census measuring both fruitless-family rates. Toy evidence is evidence at toy scope only.
